description: NaPbP₃O₉ crystallizes in the orthorhombic P2_12_12₁ space group. Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.49-2.88 Å. Pb is bonded to six O atoms to form PbO₆ octahedra that share corners with six PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Pb-O bond distances ranging from 2.49-2.65 Å. There are three inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent PbO₆ octahedra and corners with two PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 52-65°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.50-1.63 Å. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent PbO₆ octahedra and corners with two PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 59-64°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.50-1.64 Å. In the third P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent PbO₆ octahedra and corners with two PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 56-63°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.50-1.64 Å. There are nine inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to one Na, one Pb, and one P atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a bent 120 degrees geometry to two P atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Pb, and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Pb, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a bent 120 degrees geometry to two P atoms. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a bent 120 degrees geometry to two P atoms. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to one Na, one Pb, and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to one Na, one Pb, and one P atom. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one Na, one Pb, and one P atom.
